deals.evidence: Die Finanzierung der zwei Millionen Euro bringt der FCH über ein sogenanntes Schuldscheindarlehen, gegeben von institutionellen Anlegern, ein.
deals.headline: Heidenheim buys the Voith-Arena from the city for €2m, financed by a Schuldschein loan from institutional investors
deals.summary: The club bought the stadium with its five training pitches and car parks from the city for €2m, ending a lease that ran to 2039; the purchase was financed through a Schuldscheindarlehen (promissory-note loan) from unnamed institutional investors.

name: 1. FC Heidenheim 1846 e. V.
notes: Heidenheim plays in the 2. Bundesliga in 2026/27 (the club's matchcenter lists '2. Bundesliga - 6. Spieltag' on 20.09.26), i.e. it was relegated from the Bundesliga after 2025/26; the league field is left as given. Revenue is the e.V.'s calendar-year 2024 Ertrag (€89.6m; net result €1.7m after tax); the club then moved its financial year to the season and reported a short year Jan–Jun 2025 (Ertrag €41.7m, net −€271k) and a 2024/25 season net result of €956k after tax, but stated no 2024/25 season revenue on its own page (press reports of €92.46m could not be opened). Calendar 2023: Ertrag €57,775,130 (2024 members' meeting page). No pre-tax result, wages, net debt, attendance, valuation or social counts found on citable pages; no outside investor exists (member-owned e.V.). The Schuldschein lenders are not named.

owners.evidence: Er entstand 2007 durch die Abspaltung der Fußballabteilung aus dem Heidenheimer Sportbund 1846
owners.name: Members of 1. FC Heidenheim 1846 e. V.

ownership_summary: 1. FC Heidenheim 1846 is a registered members' association (e.V.), formed in 2007 when the football department split from Heidenheimer Sportbund 1846; the professional team is run by the e.V. itself, whose board reports the accounts to the members' meeting. There is no outside investor; the club honoured its 13,000th member in November 2025.
